turns.content:
All 42 tests in test_util.py pass. The fix was simple - the condition `if True:` on line 436 of `gunicorn/util.py` should have been `if not callable(app):`. This was a clear bug where the condition was hardcoded to always be True, causing the function to always raise an error that the application object must be callable, regardless of whether it actually was callable or not.

## Summary

The issue was in `/testbed/gunicorn/util.py` at line 436. The condition `if True:` was hardcoded instead of the intended `if not callable(app):`. This caused the `import_app` function to always raise an `AppImportError` claiming the application object must be callable, even when the object was actually callable.

The fix was to change:
```python
if True:  # not callable(app):
```
to:
```python
if not callable(app):
```

All 42 tests in `tests/test_util.py` now pass, including the 5 previously failing `test_import_app_good` tests.
